rule.PARSE.FAILED.explanation: {0}. The rest of the file was analyzed; this part needs a manual check.

rule.SHADER.URP.LEGACY_PASS.title: Built-in passes: {0}
rule.SHADER.URP.LEGACY_PASS.explanation: Unity reports passes with LightMode {0}. URP renders objects that use them with the error shader.
rule.SHADER.URP.LEGACY_PASS.manual: Rewrite the passes with LightMode UniversalForward.
rule.SHADER.URP.NO_DRAWN_PASS.title: No pass URP renders
rule.SHADER.URP.NO_DRAWN_PASS.explanatio: The SubShader URP selects has passes {0}. None of them is drawn by URP's forward renderer, so objects with this shader disappear.
rule.SHADER.URP.NO_DRAWN_PASS.manual: Add a pass with LightMode UniversalForward or SRPDefaultUnlit.
rule.SHADER.COMPILE_ERRORS.title: Shader already fails to compile
rule.SHADER.COMPILE_ERRORS.explanation: Unity reports {0} compile error(s) before migration. Objects with this shader are already pink; migration does not change that.
rule.SHADER.COMPILE_ERRORS.manual: Fix the compile errors in the Built-in Render Pipeline first, then scan again.
rule.SHADER.URP.ALREADY_SUPPORTED.title: Already supports URP
rule.SHADER.URP.ALREADY_SUPPORTED.explan: URP selects a SubShader tagged UniversalPipeline. No conversion needed.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.title: Surface shader, lighting {0}
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.explanation: URP does not support surface shaders: #pragma surface generates Built-in passes, and URP renders them pink. Options: {1}.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.CUSTOM_LIGHTING.expl: Lighting model {0} is the author's own function. Pro calls it once for the main light and once per additional light with URP shadows; the result is close to Built-in, not identical.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.CUSTOM_LIGHTING.manu: Function {1} was not found in the shader or its local includes. Make its include file part of the scan scope, or port the function by hand.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.TESSELLATION.title: Tessellation ({0})
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.TESSELLATION.explana: URP has no surface tessellation. Pro generates hull and domain stages from the template; the result is close to Built-in, not identical.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.FINALGBUFFER.title: finalgbuffer function
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.FINALGBUFFER.explana: The function runs only in the deferred G-buffer pass. The converted forward shader ignores it.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.UNKNOWN_OPTION.title: Unsupported surface options: {0}
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.UNKNOWN_OPTION.expla: Urpify does not translate these #pragma surface options: {0}.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.UNKNOWN_OPTION.manua: Port the behavior of {0} by hand after conversion.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.EXTRA_PASS.title: Extra passes next to the surface program ({0})
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.EXTRA_PASS.explanati: Hand-written passes such as an outline sit next to the surface program. Pro keeps them as SRPDefaultUnlit passes; the order of drawing can differ from Built-in.
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDBASE.title: ForwardBase pass
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDBASE.explanation: URP renders passes tagged ForwardBase with the error shader. Pro retags the pass UniversalForward and routes lighting, shadows and ambient through URP.
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDADD.title: ForwardAdd pass
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDADD.explanation: URP has no per-light additive pass. Pro moves additional lights into a loop in the main pass; the result is close to Built-in, not identical.
rule.SHADER.PASS.SHADOWCASTER.title: Built-in ShadowCaster pass
rule.SHADER.PASS.SHADOWCASTER.explanatio: Pro rewrites the pass for URP shadows with ApplyShadowBias so shadow bias matches URP lights.
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS.title: UsePass {0}
rule.SCRIPT.LIGHT_BUFFER_EFFECT.title: Effect fed by light command buffers ({0})
rule.SCRIPT.LIGHT_BUFFER_EFFECT.explanat: This effect draws what {0} renders with Light.AddCommandBuffer. URP does not run command buffers on lights, so under URP the effect has nothing to draw.
rule.SCRIPT.LIGHT_BUFFER_EFFECT.manual: Not supported yet: Urpify leaves the effect as it is, so it is missing under URP and the rest of the frame is drawn. Converting it needs the light's commands in a Renderer Feature.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_UNRECORDABLE.title: Effect calls code URP cannot record ({0})
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_UNRECORDABLE.explanat: OnRenderImage reaches {0}. Under URP an effect runs while URP records the frame, and this call runs at once instead, before the frame is drawn, so the converted effect would black out or blank the whole frame.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_UNRECORDABLE.manual: Not supported yet: Urpify leaves the effect as it is, so it is missing under URP and the rest of the frame is drawn. To convert it, move that call out of the effect (into OnPreRender, or into a command buffer run with ImageEffectGraphics.ExecuteCommandBuffer) and run the step again.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_GBUFFER.title: Effect reads Built-in's G-buffer ({0})
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_GBUFFER.explanation: The effect's shader: {0}. URP does not provide Built-in's G-buffer, so under URP the effect would draw from empty textures and distort the frame instead of adding the effect.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_GBUFFER.manual: Not supported yet: Urpify leaves the effect as it is, so it is missing under URP and the rest of the frame is drawn. The shader's own finding says how to rebuild its inputs for URP.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_DELEGATES.title: Camera.{0}
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_DELEGATES.explanation: Built-in calls Camera.{0} for every camera; URP never does, so the code added to it stops running, without an error.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_DELEGATES.manual: Not supported yet. Move the code to RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering (onPreCull, onPreRender) or endCameraRendering (onPostRender).
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS_MISSING.title: UsePass {0}: shader not found
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS_MISSING.explana: The pass comes from {1}, which is not in the project. Unity cannot take the pass, so the object renders pink in Built-in too. The project was broken before the migration.
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS_MISSING.manual: Add {1} to the project, or remove the UsePass line.
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS.explanation: The pass is borrowed from a Built-in shader. Pro generates an equivalent URP pass in place.
rule.SHADER.PASS.LEGACY_LIGHTMODE.title: LightMode {0}
rule.SHADER.PASS.LEGACY_LIGHTMODE.explan: URP does not use LightMode {0}. Passes tagged Always, Vertex, VertexLM or PrepassBase render pink; Deferred and PrepassFinal passes are skipped.
rule.SHADER.PASS.LEGACY_LIGHTMODE.manual: Retag the pass UniversalForward or SRPDefaultUnlit if it draws the object, or remove it if it only served the Built-in lighting path.
rule.SHADER.PASS.MULTIPLE_UNTAGGED.title: {0} passes without LightMode
rule.SHADER.PASS.MULTIPLE_UNTAGGED.expla: URP draws only the first pass without a LightMode tag. The other passes, such as an outline, disappear. Checked on URP 14 and 17.
rule.SHADER.BUILTIN_LIGHTING.title: Built-in light variable {0}
rule.SHADER.BUILTIN_LIGHTING.explanation: URP does not set {0}, so the value is zero and lighting from it disappears. Pro maps it to URP's main light.
rule.SHADER.GRABPASS.title: GrabPass ({0})
rule.SHADER.GRABPASS.explanation: URP has no GrabPass, so the object disappears or loses its refraction. Pro reads _CameraOpaqueTexture and turns on Opaque Texture. That texture is captured before transparent objects, so they are missing from the result.
rule.SHADER.DEPTH_TEXTURE.title: Reads {0}
rule.SHADER.DEPTH_TEXTURE.explanation: URP fills the depth texture only when Depth Texture is on in the URP Asset. Unity's converter turns it on only for quality levels that had Soft Particles, so effects like intersection foam disappear on the others. Urpify turns Depth Texture on in every URP Asset.
rule.SHADER.DEPTH_TEXTURE_TRANSPARENT.ex: A transparent shader reads the depth texture, but URP copies depth after transparent objects by default, and Unity's converter keeps that. In Unity 6 the shader then reads no depth: water turns white. In 2022.3 it reads the previous frame's depth: still frames look right, moving objects leave a trail. Urpify turns Depth Texture on and sets Depth Texture Mode to After Opaques.
rule.SHADER.DEPTHNORMALS_TEXTURE.title: Reads {0}
rule.SHADER.DEPTHNORMALS_TEXTURE.explana: URP has no depth-normals texture. Pro's Built-in Camera Hooks renderer feature writes {0} from URP's depth and normals textures in Built-in's encoding, so the shader reads it as before. URP's normals come from its own depth-normals pass, so edges can differ slightly.
rule.SHADER.GBUFFER_TEXTURE.title: Reads Built-in's G-buffer ({0})
rule.SHADER.GBUFFER_TEXTURE.explanation: The shader reads {0} from Built-in's deferred path. URP's Forward renderer has no G-buffer, and URP's Deferred path names and packs its own differently (_GBuffer0 to _GBuffer6), so the shader reads empty textures: the effect loses its input without an error. Checked on URP 14 and 17.
rule.SHADER.GBUFFER_TEXTURE.manual: Urpify does not convert G-buffer reads yet. Rebuild the inputs from what URP provides (depth texture, normals texture, opaque texture), or switch the URP renderer to Deferred and rewrite the reads for URP's G-buffer layout (UnityGBuffer.hlsl).
rule.SHADER.PROJECTOR.title: Projector shader ({0})
rule.SHADER.PROJECTOR.explanation: URP does not render Projector components, so this shader is never drawn. Pro draws the projectors with Urpify's renderer feature, and this shader runs unchanged.
rule.SHADER.IMAGE_EFFECT.title: Image effect shader ({0})
rule.SHADER.IMAGE_EFFECT.explanation: Used by an OnRenderImage script. The shader stays as it is: Pro runs the script's OnRenderImage under URP, and its Blit draws this shader as in Built-in.
rule.SHADER.MISSING_INCLUDE.title: Include not found: {0}
rule.SHADER.MISSING_INCLUDE.explanation: The file is not in the project and is not a Built-in include, so parts of the shader were not analyzed.
rule.SHADER.MISSING_INCLUDE.manual: Add {0} to the project or fix the path, then scan again.
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.title: OnRenderImage ({0} Blit calls)
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.explanation: URP never calls OnRenderImage, so the effect disappears without an error. Checked on URP 14 and 17. Pro runs the method under URP at {1} with Urpify's renderer feature; its Blit calls go through ImageEffectGraphics and keep their order and materials.
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.manual: The method draws immediately with {2}, which URP cannot run at this point of the frame. Draw with a command buffer instead (CommandBuffer.Blit, DrawMesh) and run it with ImageEffectGraphics.ExecuteCommandBuffer.
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.manualRender: The method renders a camera with {2}. Under URP an image effect runs inside its own camera's frame, where no other camera can render, so the effect would come out black. Render the other camera in OnPreRender or OnPreCull instead (Urpify runs them under URP before the frame) and keep only the Blit calls in OnRenderImage. A Blit that tests the camera's stencil buffer does not see it under URP either: draw the masked part with a second camera or a material on the mask itself.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_CALLBACKS.title: {0} on a camera
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_CALLBACKS.explanation: URP never calls {0}, so this code stops running. Checked on URP 14 and 17. Portals and mirrors that render a camera here show a flat surface instead. Pro calls {0} from URP's camera rendering events, and Camera.Render in it renders into URP's frame.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_CALLBACKS.manual: Subscribe to RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering or endCameraRendering and move the code there. For Camera.Render, use RenderPipeline.SubmitRenderRequest.
rule.SCRIPT.WILLRENDER_CAMERA.title: OnWillRenderObject renders a camera
rule.SCRIPT.WILLRENDER_CAMERA.explanatio: URP calls OnWillRenderObject while it culls a camera, where no other camera can render, so a mirror or water reflection rendered here stays empty. Pro calls the method before URP culls and renders the reflection camera into URP's frame.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.CAMERA.title: CommandBuffer at {0}
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.CAMERA.explana: URP ignores command buffers added to a camera, so what they draw disappears. Pro adds them with AddCommandBufferInUrp, and Urpify's renderer feature runs them at the matching URP event.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.CAMERA.manual: URP's forward renderer has no point for {0}, an event of Built-in's deferred path. Move the commands into a Renderer Feature at the matching URP event.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.LIGHT.title: CommandBuffer at {0}
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.LIGHT.explanat: URP ignores command buffers added to a light, so what they draw disappears.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.LIGHT.manual: Move the commands into a Renderer Feature at BeforeRenderingShadows or AfterRenderingShadows. URP renders shadow maps differently, so check what the commands expect.
rule.SCRIPT.REPLACEMENT_SHADER.explanati: URP does not support replacement shaders, so the camera renders nothing useful for the effect that reads it. In ToonWaterShader this removed the water foam. Pro draws the camera's opaque objects with the replacement shader in Urpify's renderer feature.
rule.SCRIPT.REPLACEMENT_SHADER.manual: Render the data with a Renderer Feature: use URP's depth or normals texture, or draw with an override material in a custom pass.
rule.SCRIPT.SHADER_FIND_BUILTIN.title: Shader.Find("{0}")
rule.SCRIPT.SHADER_FIND_BUILTIN.explanat: The code creates materials with the Built-in shader {0} at run time. Unity's converter does not touch code, so these materials render pink in URP. Urpify changes the name to the URP shader and renames properties such as _MainTex and _Color in the same script.
rule.SCRIPT.SHADER_FIND_BUILTIN.manual: Replace the shader name with a URP shader and update the property names the code sets.
rule.SCRIPT.DEPTH_TEXTURE_MODE.title: Camera.depthTextureMode
rule.SCRIPT.DEPTH_TEXTURE_MODE.explanati: URP ignores this property. Depth and normals textures come from the URP Asset settings, which Urpify turns on when shaders read them.
rule.MATERIAL.UNITY_CONVERTER.explanatio: Unity's Render Pipeline Converter has an upgrader for {0}.
rule.MATERIAL.STANDARD_TRANSPARENT.title: {0}, Transparent mode
rule.MATERIAL.STANDARD_TRANSPARENT.expla: After Unity's converter, Standard in Transparent mode turns almost opaque and white: the converter picks URP's Premultiply blending, which expects colors already multiplied by alpha. Urpify converters switch the material to Alpha blending with Preserve Specular Lighting, as Built-in blends it.
rule.MATERIAL.SELF_ILLUMIN.explanation: After Unity's converter, Legacy Self-Illumin materials lose their glow: Simple Lit takes no emission from the Illumin alpha. Urpify converters switch them to Urpify's Self-Illumin shader for URP, which glows as in Built-in.
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_NO_UPGRADER.title: {0}, no upgrader
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_NO_UPGRADER.explan: Unity's converter has no upgrader for {0} and reports it as No upgrader found. In URP: {1}.
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_NO_UPGRADER.manual: Assign a URP shader to this material by hand.
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_TREE.title: {0}, no URP version
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_TREE.explanation: URP has no Tree Creator or soft-occlusion tree shaders, so this tree renders pink. Urpify Pro converts Unity's own Built-in tree shaders for URP and move the bark and leaf materials to them. Terrain grass and detail meshes are not affected: URP draws them with its own detail shaders.
rule.MATERIAL.CUSTOM_SHADER.title: Uses {0}
rule.MATERIAL.CUSTOM_SHADER.explanation: The material keeps its values; what happens to it depends on the shader {1}. See the shader's findings.
rule.SHADER.LIBRARY_COPIES.title: Shader library {2}
rule.SHADER.LIBRARY_COPIES.explanation: The project has {0} copies of Urpify's shader library, versions {1}: its own and the UrpCompat folders of packages exported with Urpify. Each package includes its own copy, so they do not clash; newer copies may fix issues of older ones.
rule.CATALOG.KNOWN.title: Known {0}: {1}
catalog.match.exact: The same source as the catalog entry.
catalog.match.renamed: The same code with other names or property defaults.
catalog.match.similar: Looks like it: {0} % of the code in common. A hint only: Urpify converts this shader on its own, not by this entry's recipe.
observed.silentExpected: Check: a silent break was expected here. See the difference map.
observed.silentFixedCheck: Check: a silent break was expected here. The migration converted it; see the difference map to confirm.
observed.flatFrame: Check: after the migration the frame is almost one flat colour, before it was not. The screen effects of this scene ({0}) are marked Review: turn them off on the camera to find the one at fault, or roll back the migration.
observed.grabSheet: These errors come from shaders that are not converted and use GrabPass ({0}), which URP does not run: {1}. Each shader's finding says why it was not converted.
catalog.official: The author also publishes a URP version, {0} ({1}); it can be better than a conversion.
rule.SCENE.PROJECTOR.title: Projector on {0}
rule.SCENE.PROJECTOR.explanation: URP does not render Projector components, so the projected shadow or decal disappears. Pro keeps the Projector and draws it with Urpify's renderer feature, the way Built-in does.
rule.SCENE.PPV2.title: Post-processing Stack v2 on {0}
rule.SCENE.PPV2.explanation: URP does not run Post-processing Stack v2, so its effects, such as bloom, disappear without an error. Unity's converter turns PPv2 volumes and profiles into URP Volumes, but its batch mode does not wait for the search it needs and converts none of them (ShaderTutorials 050 and 051 lost bloom). Urpify's Unity converter step waits for the search. Bloom stays, with a softer, wider glow: URP's bloom spreads light differently.
rule.SCENE.PPV2.manual: If the Unity converter step reports that Post-processing v2 was not converted, run the Post-Processing Stack v2 converter from Window > Rendering > Render Pipeline Converter.
rule.SCENE.TERRAIN_BUILTIN.title: Terrain on {0}
rule.SCENE.TERRAIN_BUILTIN.explanation: The terrain uses the default material. URP switches it to its own terrain shader.
rule.SCENE.BINARY.title: Binary scene file
rule.SCENE.BINARY.explanation: The file is not text-serialized, so component-level checks (Projector, post-processing, scripts on objects) were skipped. Materials and shaders the scene uses were still checked.
rule.PROJECT.SCRIPT_COMPILATION_FAILED.e: Unity reports script compilation errors. They block entering Play Mode and running the migration steps, even though they are not caused by the render pipeline.
rule.PROJECT.SCRIPT_COMPILATION_FAILED.m: Fix the errors in the Console first. Old projects often need obsolete API calls updated.
rule.SETTINGS.URP_NOT_INSTALLED.title: URP not installed
rule.SETTINGS.URP_NOT_INSTALLED.explanat: The migration installs URP {0}.x, the version that matches this Unity Editor.
rule.SETTINGS.PPV2_PACKAGE.title: Post-processing Stack v2 {0}
rule.SETTINGS.PPV2_PACKAGE.explanation: Unity's converter turns its profiles into URP Volumes. Scenes that use it are listed with their own findings.
rule.SETTINGS.URP_ASSET_TEXTURES.title: URP Asset missing textures
rule.SETTINGS.URP_ASSET_TEXTURES.explana: The URP Asset has no {0}. URP 14 reads these textures every frame. The Editor fills them in, but a built player cannot: it throws NullReferenceException every frame and renders black. Unity's converter saves its URP Assets without them. Urpify fills them from the URP package after Unity's converter.
rule.SCENE.ENVIRONMENT_NOT_BAKED.title: Skybox ambient light not baked
rule.SCENE.ENVIRONMENT_NOT_BAKED.explana: The scene gets ambient light from the skybox but has no baked lighting data. A Unity 6 player then renders it without that light, in Built-in and in URP alike, so it looks darker than in the Editor. This is not caused by the migration. Bake environment in the scene panel bakes the ambient light and reflections, so the player matches the Editor.

rule.SCENE.BUILTIN_MATERIAL.title: {0} on {2} renderer(s)
rule.SCENE.BUILTIN_MATERIAL.explanation: Renderers such as {3} use the Editor's built-in material {0} with shader {1}. Unity's converter points them to URP's default material, which is mid-grey, not white. Seen on the ground plane in ShaderTutorials 008, 009 and 010. Urpify points them to URP copies with the built-in material's values.
rule.SCENE.PACKAGE_MATERIAL.title: Package material {0} on {3} renderer(s)
rule.SCENE.PACKAGE_MATERIAL.explanation: Renderers such as {4} use {0} from a package ({1}), whose shader {2} URP cannot draw. Packages are read-only, so Unity's converter leaves the material as it is and the renderers turn pink. Seen on ProBuilder 5's default material. Urpify points them to a URP copy in the project: Unity's own upgrader for a built-in shader, otherwise URP Lit with the material's color, texture, smoothness and metallic.
rule.SCENE.MISSING_MATERIAL.title: Missing material on {0} renderer(s)
rule.SCENE.MISSING_MATERIAL.explanation: Renderers such as {1} use a material that is not in the project (GUID {2}), so they render pink in Built-in already; the migration does not change that. It often happens when Unity upgrades a package, such as ProBuilder, whose old default material is gone.
rule.SCENE.MISSING_MATERIAL.manual: Assign a material to these renderers, or bring back the missing material or package, then scan again.
rule.SCRIPT.BUILTIN_PROPERTY_NAMES.title: Built-in property names in code
rule.SCRIPT.BUILTIN_PROPERTY_NAMES.expla: The code reads or sets {0}. On materials that Unity's converter switches to URP Lit, these names become hidden properties the shader ignores, so the calls stop changing anything. Materials with custom shaders keep the names. Pro renames them in the code for converted materials.
rule.ANIMATION.MATERIAL_PROPERTIES.title: Animates Built-in material properties ({0} curves)
rule.ANIMATION.MATERIAL_PROPERTIES.expla: The clip animates {1} and similar Built-in names. Unity's converter has an Animation Clip upgrader for them; the result is not verified by Urpify yet.
rule.MATERIAL.VARIANT.title: Material Variant of {0}
rule.MATERIAL.VARIANT.explanation: The material inherits from {0}. Unity's converter moves the parent to URP; the variant's own values (set for the Built-in shader) are carried over to the URP shader's properties after it.

ui.migrate.intro: Steps that change files back them up first. Any step can be rolled back.
ui.migrate.introTip: Each step runs on its own and can be run again. Backups go to Urpify/Backup. Roll back restores the changed files and moves the files the steps created into the same backup. Files that appear between steps are never touched.

step.Scan.title: Scan
step.Scan.what: Read-only. Lists what breaks, as in the main window.
step.CaptureBefore.title: Capture before
step.CaptureBefore.what: Plays each scene in Play Mode and saves frames from the main camera and every Migration Viewpoint.
step.Backup.title: Back up
step.Backup.what: Copies the project's assets, settings and package list to Urpify/Backup.
step.InstallUrp.title: Install URP
step.InstallUrp.what: Adds the URP version that ships with this Editor, then checks that its assemblies load.
step.UnityConverter.title: Run Unity's converter
step.UnityConverter.what: Runs the Render Pipeline Converter (Built-in to URP) and rescans to confirm the result.
step.KitConverters.title: Urpify converters
step.KitConverters.what: Fixes what Unity's converter leaves broken. Shaders, scripts and components are converted by Urpify Pro.
step.CaptureAfter.title: Capture after and compare
step.CaptureAfter.what: Captures the same frames in URP and compares them with the frames from before.
step.Review.title: Review
step.Review.what: Writes the final report: what is fixed, what differs, what needs manual work.
ui.scene.view.Same: {0}: looks the same after the migration
ui.scene.view.Pink: {0}: shows new pink after the migration
ui.scene.staticWhat: From the scan: the worst break among everything the scene uses. A pink object can be out of the captured frames.
ui.scene.observedWhat: From the captures '{0}' and '{1}': the worst frame of the scene.
ui.scene.observedNone: Run Capture before and Capture after in Migrate to compare frames.
ui.scene.pinkNotInFrame: The scan found objects that render pink, but no captured frame shows new pink. Add a Migration Viewpoint that sees these objects:
ui.scene.metrics: Pink pixels: {0}% before, {1}% after. Changed pixels: {2}%. Mean difference: {3} of 255.
ui.scene.bake.title: Ambient light
ui.scene.bake.what: Bakes the skybox's ambient light and reflections into this scene, so a Unity 6 player lights it as the Editor does.
ui.scene.bake.whatTip: Lightmaps are not baked. The project is backed up first, and the bake can be rolled back here or with Roll back in Migrate.
ui.scene.bake.undoWhat: Roll back the bake to remove the lighting data and restore the scene.
ui.scene.bake.confirmText: {0} is saved with new lighting data: ambient light and reflections from the skybox. Lightmaps are not baked, and Auto Generate is turned off for the scene. The project is backed up first, and the bake can be rolled back from the scene panel.
ui.scene.bake.undoText: The lighting data of {0} is removed, and the scene is restored as it was before the bake.
ui.bake.busy: A migration step is running. Bake after it finishes.
ui.bake.lightmapping: Unity is baking lighting. Bake after it finishes.
ui.bake.noScene: Scene {0} not found. Scan again to refresh the list.
ui.bake.cancelled: Bake cancelled: the open scenes have unsaved changes. Save them and bake again.
ui.bake.failed: Bake failed: Unity reported an error, and nothing was changed. Check the Console, fix the error and bake again.
ui.bake.noData: The bake made no lighting data, so nothing was changed. Check that the scene has a skybox material in Window > Rendering > Lighting > Environment.
ui.compare.labels: Before is left of the line, after is right of it. Show differences marks changed pixels: the larger the change, the redder the pixel.
ui.shader.convertPackage: Shaders of a package are converted when it is exported: Report > Export converted package.
ui.shader.openFailed: Can't open this shader: {0}. Check that the file exists and is a text .shader file.
ui.shader.converterError: The converter stopped with an error: {0}. Convert this shader by hand, and send the report so we can fix the converter.
ui.shader.convertTip: Replace the shader with the result below. A copy of the original goes to Urpify/Backup/ShaderPanel.
ui.shader.convertOnlyAssets: Only shaders under Assets can be converted in place. Use Save as for this one.
ui.shader.nothingToConvert: There is no converted result for this shader.
ui.shader.proNeeded: Converting shaders is part of Urpify Pro.
ui.shader.noConverter: No Urpify converter handles this shader. The scan's findings say what to change by hand.
ui.shader.rendersAsIs: URP draws this shader as it is. Nothing to convert.
ui.shader.notConverted: The converter could not convert this shader. The notes above say what to do by hand.
ui.shader.saveAsTip: Write the result to a new file and keep the original unchanged.
ui.shader.openFileTip: Open the original in your code editor.
ui.shader.convertText: Replace {0} with the converted shader? A copy of the original goes to Urpify/Backup/ShaderPanel.
ui.shader.convertFailed: The converted shader did not compile, so the original is back. Compiler: {0} (line {1}). Fix the result in the Code tab and compile it before converting.
ui.shader.convertDone: Shader converted. The original is saved at {0}.
ui.shader.savedOutside: Saved to {0}. The file is outside Assets: copy Urpify's ShaderLibrary folder next to it, or it will not compile.
ui.shader.draftStop: The converter stopped here. The note on this line says why.
ui.shader.draftNote: Draft: the converter stopped, so this result is incomplete. Lines marked with ! show where it stopped. Save as writes the draft to a new file to finish by hand. Convert and the migration never use it.
ui.shader.saveDraftTip: Write the incomplete draft to a new file to finish by hand. The original stays unchanged.
ui.shader.editTip: Show or hide the editor for the converted code.
ui.shader.compileTip: Compile the edited result for the keywords its materials use. Errors appear on their lines.
ui.shader.notImported: The shader did not import. Check the ShaderLab syntax near the first changed line.
ui.shader.why.replaced: Replaced in the result: see the matching lines on the right.
ui.shader.why.include: Shared code for all passes: URP includes, Urpify's Built-in compatibility library and the material constants.
ui.shader.why.forward: Main lighting pass for URP (UniversalForward), generated from the surface function.
ui.shader.why.shadow: Shadow caster pass, generated with the same rules Built-in uses for this shader.
ui.shader.why.depth: Depth pass URP uses for the depth texture and depth priming.
ui.shader.why.depthNormals: Depth and normals pass URP uses for SSAO and other effects.
ui.shader.why.cbuffer: Material properties moved into UnityPerMaterial so the shader works with the SRP Batcher.
ui.shader.why.compat: Built-in names (UnityCG, lighting helpers) come from Urpify's compatibility library.
ui.shader.why.pragma: The converter generates the passes this surface pragma used to generate.
ui.shader.why.builtinPragma: This pragma only works in Built-in. URP needs its own keywords, which the pass declares.
ui.shader.why.hlsl: URP programs are HLSL blocks, not CG blocks.
ui.shader.why.fallback: Built-in fallbacks don't exist in URP. The error shader shows when nothing else fits.
ui.shader.why.cginclude: Shared CG code, moved into the HLSL include block.
ui.shader.lightTip: Turn the main light around the object.
ui.shader.builtInPreviewTip: Live switches the render pipeline off for the moment of rendering and back. From captures shows the scene captures instead.
ui.shader.previewNoShader: The converted code does not load as a shader. Compile it in the Code tab to see the errors.

ui.settings.grabPassTip: Opaque Texture: URP's copy of the screen before transparent objects. After transparents: Urpify's renderer feature copies the screen after them, as Built-in's GrabPass did.
ui.settings.screenEffectsTip: Where OnRenderImage effects run in URP's frame.
ui.settings.compareFramesTip: Frames played at a fixed time step before each capture, so animation and particles are in the same state before and after.
ui.settings.compareScenesTip: Which scenes Capture before and Capture after take.
ui.settings.compareSelectedTip: Scene paths separated by semicolons, such as Assets/Scenes/Main.unity;Assets/Scenes/Menu.unity
ui.settings.compareThresholds: The thresholds for Pink, Changed and Same are calibrated on Standard to URP Lit and apply to every project.
ui.settings.overlaysTip: Mark assets the last scan found broken in the Project window.
ui.settings.languageTip: Language of the Urpify windows. Editor language follows Preferences > Languages, with English when Urpify does not have that language. Converter notes in reports stay in English.

ui.compare.title: Compare scenes

ui.send.title: Send report
ui.send.heading: Send a shader Urpify cannot convert
ui.send.noShader: Select a shader in the Urpify window first, then open Send report.
ui.send.warning: These files are your project's code. They go to Urpify's developer only to find out what the converter is missing, and are deleted after that. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
ui.send.reportFile: (findings, versions, compiler errors, your comment and contact)
ui.send.contactTip: An email address or Discord name, for questions about the shader
ui.send.sendTip: Send the archive to the support channel
ui.send.notConfigured: Send is not available: the support channel is not set up yet. Use Save zip instead and send the file by email or Discord.
ui.send.saveZipTip: Save the archive on this computer; nothing is sent
ui.send.tooSoon: Not sent: one report a minute is allowed. Try again in a minute.
ui.send.tooLarge: Not sent: the archive is {0} MB, over the {1} MB limit for Send. Use Save zip instead.
ui.send.failed: Not sent: {0}. Check the connection and try again, or use Save zip instead.
ui.overview.exportBothTip: Convert the package's shaders so one file works in both pipelines, and save a new .unitypackage with the compatibility report
ui.overview.exportBothPro: Exporting a converted package is part of Urpify Pro.
ui.settings.shadowsTip: Converted surface shaders: cast and receive shadows as the original does, always, or never.
ui.settings.srpBatcherTip: Put material properties in the UnityPerMaterial buffer so URP's SRP Batcher can batch the converted shaders.
observed.samePipeline: Nothing to compare: the frames before and after were both taken with {0}. Capture after once the project renders with URP.
step.CaptureAfter.samePipeline: Nothing to compare: both captures were taken with {0}.
step.KitConverters.whatFree: Fixes for free what Unity's converter leaves broken: glass and glowing materials, references to Built-in materials and shaders, and Shader.Find in scripts. Your own shaders, screen effects and camera scripts need Urpify Pro.
step.blocked.backupFirst: Back up the project first (step 2). Unity can re-save assets while the scenes play, and the backup has to hold them as they were.
step.blocked.beforeOnUrp: The project already renders with URP, so these frames wouldn't show how it looked in Built-in. Roll back the migration to capture them again.
step.blocked.installUrpFirst: Install URP first (step 4). This step needs the URP package.
step.blocked.unityConverterFirst: Run Unity's converter first (step 5). It switches the project to URP and upgrades Unity's own materials; this step fixes what it leaves.
step.blocked.captureBeforeFirst: Capture before first (step 3). Without frames from Built-in there's nothing to compare.
step.blocked.afterOnBuiltIn: The project still renders with Built-in, so the frames would look the same as before. Run Unity's converter first (step 5): it switches the project to URP.
ui.breaks.title: See what breaks before you fix anything
ui.breaks.text: Urpify captures your scenes in Built-in, switches the project to URP with Unity's converter alone, and captures them again. Then you decide: fix with Urpify, or roll back.
ui.breaks.tip: Backs up the project, captures the scenes, installs URP, runs Unity's converter and captures the scenes again. Everything can be rolled back.
ui.breaks.running: Showing what breaks: capturing the scenes, switching to URP, capturing them again.
ui.breaks.alreadyOnUrp: The project already renders with URP. Compare scenes shows what changed.
ui.result.fixing: Fixing with Urpify: converting, capturing the scenes again and writing the report.
